concept.title: Accessibility
concept.shortdesc: What the plugin makes accessible for you, what stays your responsibility as the author, and how to publish your own accessibility statement.

conbody.p: accessibilityWCAGThe plugin is built so that its output meets at level AA. Every build is checked with the axe-core accessibility engine in continuous integration, and the checks must pass before a change is released.

section.title: What the plugin provides

ul.li: the GOV.UK Design System's colour contrast, visible focus states, and 24 px minimum target sizes;
the plugin's own additions — the navigation tree, glossary, index, figure and table lists, search page and footer — built and tested to the same standard;
the page's language from @xml:lang, and right-to-left direction from @dir, carried through to the output.

section.p: Branding changes none of this. Every mode — neutral, iStandUK, NHS and official — is checked to the same WCAG 2.2 AA bar in CI, so the NHS and GOV.UK palettes, headers and footers all meet the contrast and target-size requirements.

section.title: What stays your responsibility
section.p: The plugin cannot make inaccessible source content accessible. When you author, you are responsible for:

ul.li: meaningful alt text on every image, and a title or desc on figures and diagrams;
a logical heading order — let topic and section titles set the hierarchy rather than styling text to look like a heading;
link text that makes sense out of context (avoid click here);
table headers marked up as headers, and simple table structures where possible;
captions or transcripts for any audio or video you embed.

section.note: Writing accessible DITA is the same discipline as writing accessible content anywhere; the plugin simply preserves the accessibility of what you give it.

section.title: Publishing your accessibility statement
section.p: accessibility statementUK public sector bodies must publish an accessibility statement — see . The plugin does not write that statement for you (only you can describe your service, its known issues, and how to report problems), but it publishes one as easily as any other page:

ol.li: write an accessibility-statement topic in DITA, using the GOV.UK as your template;
reference it from your map so it appears in the site — for a bookmap, the backmatter is a natural home: <backmatter> <topicref keyref="accessibility-statement"/> </backmatter>
link to it from wherever readers expect it — commonly the footer of every page.

section.p: Your statement can cite this plugin's WCAG 2.2 AA conformance for the framework, and add anything specific to your own content and hosting.
